title: Diameter of Binary Tree
source: canonical Diameter of Binary Tree concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: The input is the root node of a binary tree. The diameter is the number of edges on the longest path between any two nodes; the path may bend through a common ancestor and does not have to reach the root. Return the diameter. A single node has diameter 0.
constraints: the tree stays balanced enough that recursion is safe
hints: The longest path through a node equals the depth of its left subtree plus the depth of its right subtree.
The answer is the best such sum over all nodes, not just the root.
One bottom-up walk: each call returns its height and updates a running best with left height + right height.
solution: Single bottom-up walk: each node reports its height upward and folds left + right heights into a running best. O(n) time, O(depth) stack space.
failureHint: hidden tests include a single node, straight lines, and paths missing the root
